title: The Measurement
corpus_scope: ICLR 2018–2026 · all rated official reviews · a property of the system, not of any reviewer
question: If a paper's rating were repeated with another qualified reviewer, how much would it move — and how repeatable is a score really?

figures.title: The paper's share of the score: how much of a rating is the paper, not the reviewer (by year)
figures.deck: In every year, most of a score's variance is not the paper — its share holds at 0.34–0.45 (2026's coarser scale reads 0.18).

claims.statement: Across 2018–2025 the intraclass correlation sits between 0.34 and 0.45 — in every year, the majority of score variance is not the paper.

claims.derivation: the intraclass correlation for 2026 is stored directly as 0.18 (LOTTERY.years['2026'].icc)

figures.title: Your split, in context
figures.deck: Measure your own panel's spread — a wide split is not a death sentence: panels split by 8 points accept 47%, unanimous ones 30%.

claims.statement: A wide split is not a death sentence: panels split by eight points were accepted 47% of the time (a thin bin, 168 panels), while perfect unanimity was accepted 30% of the time (1,319 panels), because unanimity is most often unanimity about rejection.
claims.derivation: share of real ICLR 2026 panels (three or more rated reviews) accepted, grouped by max−min rating spread, at spread=8 vs. spread=0 (unanimous)

figures.title: The counterfactual conference: redraw every panel, count the flips
figures.deck: Redraw the panels and most borderline decisions come out as a coin toss — 58% of accepted papers, 37% of all decisions, flip on a fresh draw.

claims.statement: 37% of all 14,175 decided 2026 papers — and 58% of the accepted ones — would receive the other decision from a fresh draw.
claims.derivation: each paper's underlying value is estimated from its observed panel mean via the Fig 25a variance decomposition (shrunk toward the venue mean by panel-size reliability); a fresh same-size panel is redrawn and the venue's empirical P(accept | panel mean) makes the call, averaged over 4,000 redraws

claims.statement: Peaking at 54% near a mean of 5.75.
claims.derivation: maximum of the flip-probability curve P(different decision | panel mean) over 4,000 redraws

caveats.text: The rating scale changed four times across 2018–2026 (including a 4-point 2020 scale and 2026's even-only 0–10-by-2 scale). Cross-year comparisons of score-derived statistics like the intraclass correlation can be mechanically shifted by the scale's own coarseness, independent of any real change in reviewing behavior — 2026's lower ICC (0.18 vs. 0.34–0.45) should not be over-read as a real drop, and 2020's four-point form carries a milder dose of the same coarseness.

This measures the system's precision under its constraints, not any panel's diligence, and is not a validation against a real second committee: the NeurIPS consistency experiments used real independent committees and found roughly half of accepted papers un-reproduced, which this model's range is reassuringly close to but does not confirm, since one is a real experiment and the other a simulation built from this atlas's own variance estimate.
